args.command:
# sar only has system-wide data. Let's create a quick memory monitoring script
# and check if we can get any historical per-process data
# First, let's check the nanobot gateway log for any memory-related entries
grep -i -E 'memory|mem|oom|gc|garbage' /root/.nanobot/gateway.log 2>/dev/null | tail -20

# Write a quick monitoring script that samples memory every 5 minutes for 1 hour
# to detect memory growth trend
cat > /tmp/nanobot_mem_monitor.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
PID=$(pgrep -f "nanobot gateway" | head -1)
if [ -z "$PID" ]; then echo "nanobot not running"; exit 1; fi
LOG="/tmp/nanobot_mem_history.log"
echo "=== Memory monitoring started at $(date) ===" >> "$LOG"
echo "Timestamp,PID,VmRSS_kb,VmSize_kb,VmSwap_kb,Threads,RSS_MB" >> "$LOG"
for i in $(seq 1 12); do
    if ! kill -0 $PID 2>/dev/null; then echo "Process died at $(date)" >> "$LOG"; break; fi
    read rss size swap threads < <(awk '/VmRSS/{r=$2}/VmSize/{s=$2}/VmSwap/{w=$2}/Threads/{t=$2}END{print r,s,w,t}' /proc/$PID/status)
    ts=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
    rss_mb=$((rss/1024))
    echo "$ts,$PID,$rss,$size,$swap,$threads,$rss_mb" >> "$LOG"
    echo "$ts: RSS=${rss_mb}MB"
    sleep 300
done
echo "=== Monitoring ended at $(date) ===" >> "$LOG"
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/nanobot_mem_monitor.sh
echo "Script created. Starting background monitor..."
nohup /tmp/nanobot_mem_monitor.sh > /tmp/nanobot_mem_monitor.out 2>&1 &
echo "PID: $!"
grep -i "memory\|RSS\|MEM\|分配\|占用" /root/.nanobot/workspace/nanobot_stdout.log 2>/dev/null | tail -20

# Check current nanobot process start time and get a 2nd measurement for comparison
CURRENT_MEM=$(ps -o rss= -q 506698)
START_TIME=$(ps -o lstart= -q 506698)
ELAPSED=$(ps -o etime= -q 506698)
echo "Current RSS: ${CURRENT_MEM}KB (${CURRENT_MEM}KB)"
echo "Started: $START_TIME"
echo "Elapsed: $ELAPSED"
echo "---"
# Also check if there was a restart recently
grep -c "restart\|kill\|SIGTERM\|SIGINT" /root/.nanobot/workspace/nanobot_stdout.log 2>/dev/null | tail -5

# Check if there's any existing memory history or if we can get a trend from the process start
# Also check Python GC stats and object counts
python3 -c "
import subprocess, json
# Get current memory
result = subprocess.run(['cat', '/proc/506698/status'], capture_output=True, text=True)
for line in result.stdout.split('\n'):
    if any(k in line for k in ['VmRSS', 'VmSize', 'VmSwap', 'VmPeak', 'VmHWM', 'VmData', 'VmStk', 'Threads']):
        print(line)
"

# Check VmPeak (historical max) vs current to see if memory has grown
cat /proc/506698/status | grep -E 'VmPeak|VmHWM|VmRSS|VmSize'

# VmPeak was 6GB and VmHWM was 4GB but current is only 695MB RSS
# This means memory was MUCH higher at some point and got released (GC or restart of components)
# Let's check the memory breakdown more carefully
cat /proc/506698/smaps_rollup 2>/dev/null
echo "==="
# Check memory maps summary
cat /proc/506698/maps | awk '{print $6}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20
grep -E "VmPeak|VmRSS|VmSize|VmHWM" /proc/506698/status 2>/dev/null

# Check if nanobot has any built-in memory tracking or if there's a way to see memory over time
# Also check dmesg for OOM events
dmesg | grep -i -E 'oom|out of memory|kill' 2>/dev/null | tail -10
echo "==="
# Check journalctl for nanobot related memory issues
journalctl -u nanobot --no-pager -n 20 2>/dev/null || echo "No systemd unit found"

# Check if there are any older nanobot process instances that ran before
# and look for smaps memory tracking
diff -u /dev/null /dev/null 2>/dev/null; echo "---"
# Check if we can find any historical process memory data in db
find /root/.nanobot/ -name "*.db" -o -name "*.sqlite" 2>/dev/null | head -10

# Read detailed memory stats
cat /proc/506698/status | grep -E "VmRSS|VmHWM|VmPeak|VmSwap|Threads"
echo "---"
# Read smaps_rollup for PSS
cat /proc/506698/smaps_rollup 2>/dev/null | grep -E "Pss|Rss|Swap" | head -10
echo "---"
# Check if RSS has been stable by polling a few times
for i in 1 2 3; do
  RSS=$(ps -o rss= -q 506698)
  echo "Poll $i: RSS=${RSS}KB ($(date +%H:%M:%S))"
  sleep 0.5
done

# Check if there's a previous process memory record in request logs
ls -la /root/.nanobot/request_logs/ | tail -5
# Check if today's log has any memory data
grep -c "nanobot_request" /root/.nanobot/request_logs/2026-05-19.jsonl 2>/dev/null
